record.title: The Refuge Residence Rule In Two Editions
record.summary: The KJV includes a rule about staying until the high priest dies. The old Greek translation lacks that rule here.
record.text:
packaged KJV, Joshua 20:4: “And when he that doth flee unto one of those cities shall stand at the entering of the gate of the city, and shall declare his cause in the ears of the elders of that city, they shall take him into the city unto them, and give him a place, that he may dwell among them.” Source: https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JOS20.htm
packaged KJV, Joshua 20:5: “And if the avenger of blood pursue after him, then they shall not deliver the slayer up into his hand; because he smote his neighbour unwittingly, and hated him not beforetime.” Source: https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JOS20.htm
packaged KJV, Joshua 20:6: “And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, and until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days: then shall the slayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.” Source: https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JOS20.htm
Brenton Greek edition, Joshua 20:3: “Φυγαδευτήριον τῷ φονευτῇ τῷ πατάξαντι ψυχὴν ἀκουσίως· καὶ ἔσονται ὑμῖν αἱ πόλεις φυγαδευτήριον, καὶ οὐκ ἀποθανεῖται ὁ φονευτὴς ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγχιστεύοντος τὸ αἷμα, ἕως ἂν καταστῇ· ἐναντίον τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰς κρίσιν.” Source: https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JOS20.htm
Brenton Greek edition, Joshua 20:7: “Καὶ διέστειλε τὴν Κάδης ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Νεφθαλὶ, καὶ Συχὲμ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Ἐφραὶμ, καὶ τὴν πόλιν Ἀρβὸκ, αὕτη ἐστὶ Χεβρὼν, ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Ἰούδα.” Source: https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JOS20.htm
Brenton Greek edition, Joshua 20:9: “Αὗται αἱ πόλεις αἱ ἐπίκλητοι τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ καὶ τῷ προσηλύτῳ τῷ προσκειμένῳ ἐν αὐτοῖς, καταφυγεῖν ἐκεῖ παντὶ παίοντι ψυχὴν ἀκουσίως, ἵνα μὴ ἀποθάνῃ ἐν χειρὶ τοῦ ἀγχιστεύοντος τὸ αἷμα, ἕως ἄν καταστῇ ἔναντι τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰς κρίσιν.” Source: https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JOS20.htm
Brenton English translation, Joshua 20:3: “Even a refuge to the slayer who has smitten a man unintentionally; and the cities shall be to you a refuge, and the slayer shall not be put to death by the avenger of blood, until he have stood before the congregation for judgment.” Source: https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/JOS20.htm
Brenton English translation, Joshua 20:7: “And Joshua separated Cades in Galilee in the mount Nephthali, and Sychem in the mount Ephraim, and the city of Arboc; this is Chebron, in the mountain of Juda.” Source: https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/JOS20.htm
Brenton English translation, Joshua 20:9: “These were the cities selected for the sons of Israel, and for the stranger abiding among them, that every one who smites a soul unintentionally should flee thither, that he should not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he should stand before the congregation for judgment.” Source: https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/JOS20.htm
record.reasoning: The Greek page prints verses 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9. It includes judgment before the community but omits the high priest’s death as the condition for returning home.
record.scope: This comparison concerns Joshua 20:6 in these editions. The Greek’s shorter chapter does not prove the rule was unknown elsewhere. Numbers 35:25-28 also gives the residence rule. The comparison does not establish which form is earlier or whether all ancient copies agree.

record.title: A Secret Message Or An Accusation About Truth
record.summary: The KJV describes a message secretly received. The old Greek translation first questions whether the listener’s words contained any truth.
record.text:
packaged KJV, Job 4:12: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof.” Source: https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JOB04.htm
Brenton Greek edition, Job 4:12: “Εἰ δέ τι ῥῆμα ἀληθινὸν ἐγεγόνει ἐν λόγοις σου, οὐθὲν ἄν σοι τούτων κακὸν ἀπήντησε· πότερον οὐ δέξεταί μου τὸ οὖς ἐξαίσια παρʼ αὐτοῦ;” Source: https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JOB04.htm
Brenton English translation, Job 4:12: “But if there had been any truth in thy words, none of these evils would have befallen thee. Shall not mine ear receive excellent revelations from him?” Source: https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/JOB04.htm
record.reasoning: The Greek links the listener’s suffering to the truth of his words, adding a specific accusation.
record.scope: The comparison concerns Job 4:12 in these editions. It does not settle the Hebrew wording or identify the earliest form. A digital edition does not show that all ancient copies agree. This is poetic speech, not an independent account of physical events.
